ON SULPHUR.

<meta>continues from previous page: which</meta> cooked by nature, you will be able to perfect everything from Mercury. But if you know how to add your weight to the weight of nature, doubling the Mercury and tripling the sulphur, the result will more quickly reach goodness, then into something better, until it becomes the best. Although there is only one apparent sulphur and two Mercuries, they are of one root; they are neither raw nor overcooked, yet they are purified and dissolved, if you have understood me.

There is truly no need to describe the material of the Philosophers' Mercury and the material of their sulphur. No mortal has been able, nor will be able in the future, to describe it more openly and clearly than it has been described and named by the ancient Philosophers, unless one wishes to be anathema <note>a formal curse or exclusion</note> to the art. It is named so commonly that it is not even valued. Therefore, seekers turn themselves to other subtleties rather than remaining in the simplicity of nature. <summary>This page discusses the necessity of balancing Mercury and sulphur in alchemical processes, while criticizing those who overlook the simplicity of the materials described by ancient authorities.</summary>
